source.snippet: I'm trying to maintain a consistent monthly budget, but my income doesn't follow a predictable schedule — some months I earn more, some months less, and payments often arrive mid-month or late. Most budgeting advice assumes a fixed monthly paycheck, but that doesn't apply to me. I've tried: Budgeting based on last month's income; Setting a 'baseline' minimum income and ignoring anything above it; Rolling surplus from good months into a buffer account.

problem_statement: Freelancers and independent contractors cannot use mainstream budgeting tools because every tool assumes a fixed monthly salary; managing cash flow across feast-and-famine income cycles remains an unsolved, time-consuming problem.
target_segment: Freelancers, independent contractors, and gig workers with variable monthly income, particularly those earning $3k–$15k/month
notes: Existing paid market validates buyer willingness: YNAB ($99/yr), Copilot ($95/yr), Quickbooks Self-Employed ($15/mo) all have paying freelancer customers but none handle irregular income timing well — this is a recurring complaint on r/freelance, r/personalfinance, and money.stackexchange. Buyer is a freelancer actively losing money or stress to cash-flow uncertainty. Weak single signal here but corroborated by known pattern. Signal strength kept at 2 due to this batch having only one post.
